title: Christ Restores All Things
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Christ restores all things means that the final hope of redemption is not mere self-improvement, but the Lord Jesus making all things new. He will fully restore His people, judge evil, defeat death, and dwell with His redeemed forever.
summary: Christ restores all things means that the final hope of redemption is not mere self-improvement, but the Lord Jesus making all things new. He will fully restore His people, judge evil, defeat death, and dwell with His redeemed forever.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the Restorer of all things. Through His death, resurrection, reign, and return, He brings God’s redemptive purpose to completion and makes all things new.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Restoration in Scripture reaches farther than personal improvement. God’s redemptive purpose includes sinners forgiven, bodies raised, creation renewed, evil judged, death destroyed, and God dwelling with His people.

Christ is central to this restoration. Through Him, God reconciles, renews, gathers, and completes His purpose. No part of final hope exists apart from the crucified, risen, and returning Lord.

The present experience of restoration is real but partial. Believers are forgiven, renewed, and changed now, yet they still wait for final resurrection and the restoration of all things.

When Christ makes all things new, sorrow, death, crying, pain, corruption, and curse will be gone. This is the final horizon of hope for every suffering, recovering, wounded, and weary believer.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often settle for small hopes: feeling better, fixing circumstances, or improving behavior. Those gifts can matter, but Scripture gives a greater hope—Christ restoring all things.

This doctrine carries the heart of Restored Daily Ministries. The broken are not merely patched; in Christ, God is moving toward full restoration, resurrection, and eternal life with Him.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Let the final restoration in Christ shape your present hope. Do not make temporary relief your only horizon. Seek healing, growth, and faithfulness now, while looking for the day when Jesus will make all things new and every tear will be wiped away.
